research.title: DISCERN
research.description:
Lyu, S.-J. (2026). When Metrics Lie: A Protocol for Uncovering Flawed Human-Likeness in Team Shooters (Version 0.1.0). Zenodo.

A screening protocol that tests the discriminant validity of team-shooter behavioral metrics via within-series pairing, a priori direction registration, and five self-checks. Applied to 11 metrics from 1,558 professional CS:GO demos, only 3 passed (one still mechanically confounded), 2 reversed direction, and perceptual asymmetry could not be measured because visibility fields were unreliable—showing that metrics must be screened before building human-like agents, and that a controlled environment is a practical necessity.

research.title: Symbolic-Space
research.description:
Proposes validating coverage, collapse, and predicate sharpness before adopting a tactical-command vocabulary, measured on 28 verbs and 7,936 legal messages from 270 professional CS:GO matches.
The action space can express 87.7–89.2% of kills; symbolization retains about 1,305–1,533 valid utility uses and 31–32 reachable objectives, and overturns seven unchecked specification claims.
